ideas.title: Build the smallest deployable agent first
ideas.post_angle: For a first production pass, make the agent work end to end before adding structured outputs, more tools, conversation memory, or a vector database.
ideas.why_worth_posting: The audience often overbuilds agent prototypes before there is a working backend, frontend, container, and deployment path. This idea gives a concrete order of operations.

source_moments.note: The notebook has to become a proper Python project and FastAPI backend before deployment.
Structured output is useful later, but it adds complexity when combined with streaming.
The working app is packaged into one container for deployment.

clip.title: Make it work end to end first
clip.reason: This section states the trade-off clearly: ship the full path first, improve the agent later.
clip.trim_notes: Start when structured output is mentioned; end after the make-it-work-first conclusion.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a practical post for AI engineers explaining why the first milestone should be a deployed vertical slice: simple agent loop, backend, frontend, Docker, deploy. Mention that structured outputs, better retrieval, memory, and nicer UX can follow once the full path works.

ideas.title: Make agent tool use visible in the UI
ideas.post_angle: An agent UI should show streaming progress, tool calls, parameters, and tool results instead of waiting silently for the final answer.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is a concrete observability lesson for agent products. It connects backend event handling with user trust and debugging.

source_moments.note: FastAPI exposes an ask stream endpoint and sends events to the frontend.
The initial frontend waits for the final response, so Alexey asks for streaming events and visible tool calls.
The result works well enough after adding streaming and tool event visibility.

clip.title: Show tool calls as they happen
clip.reason: This is a concise explanation of why waiting for the final response is not enough.
clip.trim_notes: Use the explanation of wanting streaming API, tool calls, parameters, and collapsible tool results.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a post for AI engineers about exposing agent internals in the product UI: stream tokens, show tool calls, show inputs and outputs, collapse noisy results, and make progress observable.

ideas.title: Use one Docker image for a small agent app
ideas.post_angle: For a small agent application, one Docker image can serve the built frontend and the FastAPI backend. A multi-stage build keeps Node.js out of the runtime image.
ideas.why_worth_posting: Many learners struggle with whether they need separate frontend and backend containers. This gives a useful deployment pattern and a real debugging note about environment variables.

source_moments.note: The app is packaged as one Docker container that builds the frontend and serves static files from FastAPI.
The multi-stage build is explained: frontend build output is copied into the backend image.
A Docker environment variable issue appears because the API key is not propagated as expected.

clip.reason: The explanation answers a real participant question and works as a standalone technical clip.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a practical post explaining when one container is enough for a small agent app, how a multi-stage Docker build works, and why environment variables should be tested inside the container.

ideas.title: Keep production deployment behind CI/CD
ideas.post_angle: Coding agents can help experiment with deployment, but production should be protected by CI/CD, separate environments, tests, manual promotion, and limited credentials.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is the strongest production safety lesson in the video. It includes a real incident, a deployment model, and specific guardrails.

source_moments.note: Alexey describes not keeping AWS credentials on the remote server and mentions a production database deletion incident.
The recommended setup uses separate dev/prod environments, tests, automatic dev deploys, manual production promotion, and CI/CD.
Tests should run before deployment, with fast unit tests and CI integration tests.
The transcript includes a warning not to paste tokens into an agent conversation.

clip.reason: The anecdote is specific, memorable, and naturally supports the CI/CD safety post.

ideas.writing_brief: Write a production engineering post about using coding agents for learning and experimentation while keeping real deployment behind CI/CD, separate dev/prod environments, tests, manual approval, and secrets management.

ideas.title: Run coding agents where the work can continue
ideas.post_angle: For long-running coding-agent work, a remote machine plus tmux keeps work alive when the laptop disconnects, closes, or moves networks.
ideas.why_worth_posting: This is a practical workflow post for engineers who are starting to use coding agents for longer tasks.

source_moments.note: Alexey introduces tmux to keep the session running when SSH is interrupted.
He explains how an SSH-attached process dies and how tmux lets it continue.
A remote environment is useful for long-running bots and agent sessions.
